title: Straight dovetail
description: J01 interlocks across the Z sliding direction. The joint remains free along Z; a product may need a stop or an additional retainer on that axis.
parameters: Flanks approximately 15°, engagement 8 mm; constant profile over a height of 20 mm.
limits: No protection against sliding out along Z; thin socket cheeks may spread.

title: Tapered dovetail
description: The side faces taper along the assembly path. The smaller section enters first; further insertion reduces the available clearance. Preload and self-locking can only be assessed with actual contact and friction.
parameters: As J01, with an additional 0.5° profile taper.
limits: A print that is too tight may jam before reaching its final position; one that is too loose produces no preload.

title: Scarf dovetail
description: A shared shear transformation inclines the parting face and the slider. Both partners remain derived from the same master; drawing two separate inclined profiles would be more prone to error.
parameters: J02 with an X shear of 1.5·Z, centred about the midplane; the outer end faces are also inclined.
limits: An independent variant, not a dimensionally identical reconstruction of the original scarf. Print orientation and inclined end faces require separate consideration.

title: Curved dovetail
description: The guide follows a circular arc. A straight pulling movement meets the undercut; assembly and removal require a defined rotation. The surrounding geometry limits the sweep clearance.
parameters: Base radius 18 mm; 13 loft sections; 0.5° profile taper along the arc; end stop.
assembly: Rotate A to −77°, approach from the left, then rotate to 0° about Z at (−18, 0).
limits: Rotating as far as −110° causes a collision. The permitted approach is checked separately from the rotation alone.

title: Conical curved dovetail
description: In addition to the curved guide, the base radius changes over the height. This creates more complex contact surfaces in three dimensions. The example demonstrates the modelling method; it establishes no strength advantage.
parameters: Bottom radius 18 mm, top radius 22 mm; mean radius 20 mm; the same taper along the arc as J04.
assembly: Rotate A to −77°, approach from the left, then rotate to 0° about Z at (−20, 0).
limits: More complex printing and fit checks; the source video also treats this form as an experiment.

title: Echo-Lock principle
description: A central dovetail is accompanied by two flanks that engage in the opposite direction. Their purpose is to geometrically limit socket opening. Actual load sharing depends on fit and stiffness; it is not automatically uniform.
parameters: Central taper +1.5°; the two opposing flanks −1.5°; a shared assembly path.
limits: More undercuts also create more thin roots. A comparative load test remains outstanding.

title: Drop-Lock principle
description: Three fingers on A and two on B interleave. Their heads use true circular arcs with tangent flanks. Opposing tapers allow a shared insertion path.
parameters: Bottom head radius 2.4 mm; spacing between fingers on the same side 9 mm; draft +1°/−1°.
limits: An independent straight teaching variant; the later inclined development in the video is not included. Finger roots remain critical.

title: Stopped scarf with opposing wedges
description: The two bar ends interlock through steps and a long inclined face. Two printed wedges, oriented in opposite directions, sit in a shared transverse channel. Sliding them against each other can fill the available space.
parameters: Four bodies; bar 120 × 28 × 20 mm; two 40 mm wedges at 2°; defined scarf and wedge clearances.
assembly: Join A and B sideways, then insert the wedges. To release, push the lower wedge along +Y and the upper wedge along −Y.
limits: A deliberately simplified straight scarf section: the 45° plane and centring cones from the video are absent. Without additional lateral guidance, Y retention is not secured. The modelled final position includes clearance and does not represent measured preload.
